warnings: task_input_warnings flag: 'extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named' — verify that the extraction schema field names and model are correctly mapped to influenza, not hantavirus, before ingestion.

task_input_warnings flag: 'source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic' — source discovery logic may not yet be tuned for influenza-specific sources; manually verify CDC FluView and state health department sources are in scope.

Early-season timing (MMWR Week 40, early October 2024) means influenza activity in the United States is typically at baseline or minimal — absence of high case counts is expected and should not be treated as a data gap.
CDC FluView data for Week 40 (ending 2024-10-05) may not be publicly released until approximately 2024-10-11 — check for publication lag before flagging as missing.
State health department reporting cadences vary; some states report weekly, others biweekly or monthly — document reporting frequency per source.
Influenza surveillance data is often preliminary at time of first release and subject to revision — flag all early-season extractions as provisional.
Do not invent or infer URLs; source_url must be populated only from directly observed source documents during collection.
FluSurv-NET hospitalization data for early season weeks may have suppressed cells (counts <10) — record suppression status rather than imputing zeros.

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Coverage is good for the task window. National-level U.S. influenza surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29–Oct 5, 2024) is anchored by the CDC FluView report, which provides virological breakdown (56 influenza A viruses; 55.8% H1N1pdm09, 44.2% H3N2), percent positivity stability, ED visit trends, and a note on two H5 human cases in California. Subnational coverage is partially addressed by the Mississippi MSDH Week 40 PDF (ILI rate 2.8%, up from 2.3% prior week). PAHO Week 40 bulletin provides regional context for North America. ECDC CDTR covers the exact date range. News/specialist outlets (cidrap, contagionlive, reuters, etc.) are present in the accepted candidate pool and may yield additional evidence quotes. Gaps remain for: (a) explicit hospitalization counts (FluSurv-NET quantitative rates not confirmed in snippets); (b) confirmed deaths for the specific week; (c) subnational data beyond Mississippi. These gaps are consistent with the nature of early-season Week 40 data, where activity is at low/baseline levels and detailed hospitalization/mortality tables may not yet be populated.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High. The primary source (CDC FluView 2024-week-40.html) is from the gold-standard U.S. influenza surveillance system on the cdc.gov domain. The MSDH PDF is from an official state health department (msdh.ms.gov) with explicit Week 40 dating. PAHO (paho.org) is an authoritative WHO regional office. ECDC (ecdc.europa.eu) is an authoritative EU public health agency. News/specialist sources (cidrap.umn.edu, reuters.com, contagionlive.com) are credible secondary sources. Low-trust results (facebook.com, wikipedia, statista) are present in the accepted pool but should be deprioritized or excluded during evidence extraction. The JMIR and PMC articles are peer-reviewed but cover prior seasons, not the specific task window.
